critique.good: Part numbers and suppliers stay intact, and the compact quantity and price columns are easy to scan. The description has enough space for most rows to read in two or three lines.
critique.problems: The two-line Unit price header makes the header as tall as many data rows. The diode description splits SOT-23-6 across lines, and several descriptions leave substantial empty space in the purchasing columns.
critique.cause: The 86px price column leaves only 65px for text, too little for its header. The 241px description column leaves 220px for text, causing technical phrases to wrap.

critique.good: The wider description column produces a compact table and keeps most descriptions to two lines, making rows easier to scan across.
critique.problems: Two long part numbers split across lines, and STMicroelectronics splits mid-word in two rows. Murata via Mouser also wraps. These breaks make identification and sourcing harder despite the shorter table; the price header still wraps.
critique.cause: The 175px part-number column leaves 154px for text, and the 154px supplier column leaves 133px; both are narrower than their longest unbreakable entries. The 86px price column is too narrow for its header.

critique.good: All headers, part numbers and supplier names stay on one line. The compact header establishes a clear hierarchy, and the purchasing columns are easy to compare.
critique.problems: Descriptions wrap heavily: the microcontroller occupies four lines, while the LED and header descriptions take three. The resulting tall rows create large blank areas in the other columns and slow comparison across rows.
critique.cause: The 101px price column keeps its header intact, but leaves only 226px for Description, or 205px of text width.

critique.good: Part numbers, prices, and supplier names remain intact. The purchasing columns are compact, and the rows remain easy to follow across the table.
critique.problems: The Unit price header wraps, making the header disproportionately tall. Some descriptions divide technical expressions across lines, including SOT-23-6.
critique.cause: The 86px price column leaves 65px for text, less than the 78px needed for its header. The 241px description column leaves 220px for text.

critique.good: The wider description column gives some specifications more room, while part numbers and prices remain intact.
critique.problems: STMicroelectronics splits across lines twice, and Murata via Mouser wraps. The extra description width does not reduce the overall row heights; the Unit price header still wraps.
critique.cause: The 154px supplier column leaves only 133px for text, less than the 148px needed for the longest supplier name. The price column remains 86px wide.

critique.good: All headers fit on one line, creating a compact, clear header. Supplier names and prices remain intact.
critique.problems: Two capacitor part numbers lose their final D to a second line, making exact identification harder. Descriptions also have less room than in r1A.
critique.cause: The 195px part-number column leaves 174px for text, short of the 184px needed. The 101px price column gains a one-line header at the expense of the identifier and description columns.

critique.good: All headers, part numbers, prices, and supplier names remain intact. The compact header and consistent alignment make the purchasing columns easy to scan.
critique.problems: The microcontroller description reaches four lines, leaving a short final line and making that row conspicuously tall. Several other descriptions also occupy three lines, creating large empty areas in the neighboring cells.
critique.cause: The 228px Description column leaves 207px for text. The 99px Unit price column keeps its header on one line but takes space that could help the descriptions.

critique.good: The wider Description column reduces the microcontroller description to three lines and gives the body a more even rhythm. Part numbers, prices, and supplier names remain intact.
critique.problems: The two-line Unit price header makes the entire header row tall. Some technical expressions wrap awkwardly, including SOT-23-6 across lines and the number and unit in 16 V across lines.
critique.cause: The 86px Unit price column leaves only 65px for text, too little for the full header. The 241px Description column is still narrow enough to force breaks within some multi-part technical expressions.

understanding.purpose: Specify the components needed to build a prototype controller board, including quantities, prices and sources.
understanding.reading: Readers identify each part, check its specifications, then scan quantity, unit price and supplier for purchasing. Each row should remain easy to follow across the table.
groups: Part number and Description identify and characterize each component.
Qty and Unit price are compact purchasing figures that readers may compare down their columns.
Supplier completes the purchasing information for each part.
keep_intact: Part numbers and supplier names should remain intact where possible, because breaks make exact identification and sourcing harder.
Quantities, individual prices and technical values should remain intact.
Keep the Unit price header on one line where space permits.
may_wrap: Descriptions can wrap naturally at spaces and punctuation; longer descriptions will create row height that can absorb wrapping in other cells.
The Unit price header can wrap if that space is more valuable to descriptions.
If necessary, long part numbers or supplier names may break, with a cost to scanning and exact identification.

bad.why: STMicroelectronics breaks across lines twice, making the supplier column harder to scan.
Two part numbers lose their final character onto a separate line, making exact identifiers harder to read and check.
STMicroelectronics breaks twice, leaving a single letter on each continuation line.
STMicroelectronics breaks twice, leaving a single letter on each continuation line.

final.rationale: r1A and r2B are identical and keep part numbers, supplier names, quantities and prices intact while giving descriptions enough width to stay within three lines. The wrapped Unit price header is a reasonable cost for that allocation, though the SOT-23-6 designation still breaks at a hyphen. r2A keeps every header on one line but gives up description width, producing a four-line row and a taller table.

general: Give exact identifiers enough width to remain intact when readers must distinguish or transcribe them.
Allocate width according to content and reading purpose; a short numeric column need not match a descriptive column.
Judge wrapping by where it occurs and how it affects scanning, not by table height alone.
specific: The longest part number and supplier name set tight minimum widths of about 205px and 169px including padding.
The available width forces a choice between a wrapped Unit price header and a narrower description column if both long identifiers are kept intact.

final.tradeoffs: A designer may prefer r2A's single-line headers despite its longer descriptions, or r3A's slightly different description breaks despite its extra table height. The preferred design favors intact identifiers and a compact description column over a single-line Unit price header.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative point estimates, not measured tolerance intervals. At the full width budget, changing one column requires adjusting others; untested reallocations may be equally good.

A.why: Part numbers remain intact and the description has useful room, but STMicroelectronics breaks inside the word and the unit price header wraps.

B.why: Headers, part numbers and suppliers stay intact, but the narrower description splits LQFP-48 and creates several tall rows.

C.why: Part numbers, prices and suppliers stay intact, and descriptions are reasonably compact; the unit price header wraps and SOT-23-6 breaks across lines.

D.why: Equal column widths give excess space to quantity and price while splitting part numbers and suppliers and forcing descriptions into many short lines.

E.why: Part numbers and suppliers stay intact and SOT-23-6 fits on one line, but the narrower description breaks through-hole and lengthens the LED row; the unit price header wraps.

F.why: The width distribution keeps part numbers, suppliers and prices intact and descriptions relatively compact; SOT-23-6 and the unit price header wrap.

reviews.unsure: C and F are visually very close; their small width differences do not produce a clear overall winner. B keeps the price header on one line, but its longer description wrapping is a tradeoff.

A.why: Equal column widths leave excessive space for quantities and prices while splitting part numbers, supplier names, and descriptions across many lines.

B.why: Part numbers stay intact and descriptions have room, but supplier names split inside words and the unit-price header wraps.

C.why: Part numbers, supplier names, prices, and headers stay intact. The narrower description column produces several longer rows and splits LQFP-48.

D.why: Part numbers and suppliers stay intact, and descriptions generally wrap cleanly. The unit-price header wraps and through-hole splits across lines.

E.why: The proportions keep part numbers and suppliers intact and give descriptions useful space, though the unit-price header wraps and SOT-23-6 splits.

F.why: Identifiers and suppliers stay intact, with a clear balance between descriptions and numeric columns. The unit-price header wraps and SOT-23-6 splits.

reviews.unsure: D and E are close: D keeps SOT-23-6 together, while E keeps through-hole together and gives the LED description one fewer line. C preserves the unit-price header on one line but gives descriptions less room.
